title: Injected-clock token buckets with atomic batches
instructions:
Implement `token_bucket.py` and `rate_limiter.py`. No real clock, sleeps, threads, or background work. Use float arithmetic with exact `>=` sufficiency checks (no epsilon). Tests use modest finite values with representable boundary cases.

In this task a numeric argument is a built-in int or float, excluding bool, and must be finite unless explicitly stated otherwise. Invalid arguments raise `ValueError`; messages are unrestricted.

`token_bucket.TokenBucket(capacity: float, refill_rate: float, now: float)` requires capacity > 0, refill_rate >= 0, and finite numeric now (negative initial times are allowed). It starts full. Expose public attributes `capacity`, `refill_rate`, `tokens`, `updated_at`, stored as floats; callers do not modify them. Methods:
- `advance(now: float) -> float`: require numeric now >= updated_at. Add `(now - updated_at) * refill_rate`, cap at capacity, set updated_at to now, and return tokens. Equal timestamps are allowed. Invalid/backward time raises `ValueError` without changing state.
- `try_take(cost: float, now: float) -> bool`: cost must be numeric and > 0, with no upper bound restriction. Validate cost before time; then advance. If tokens >= cost, subtract cost and return True; otherwise return False without subtracting. A denied request still advances/refills the bucket.
- `wait_time(cost: float, now: float) -> float`: same validation and advance, but never consume. Return 0.0 if enough tokens; otherwise `(cost - tokens) / refill_rate`. Return `math.inf` if cost > capacity, or if insufficient and refill_rate is zero. Invalid inputs to either method change no state.

`rate_limiter.RateLimiter(capacity: float, refill_rate: float, clock: Callable[[], float])` uses one independent lazily created TokenBucket per key. Validate capacity/rate as above at construction; do not call clock during construction. Keys must be nonempty strings (whitespace strings are allowed); invalid keys raise `ValueError`. New keys start full at the current sampled time. Implement:
- `consume(key: str, cost: float = 1) -> bool`: advance/refill that key and attempt to consume cost.
- `retry_after(key: str, cost: float = 1) -> float`: advance/refill and return wait time without consuming.
- `available(key: str) -> float`: advance/refill and return current tokens without consuming.
- `consume_many(requests: list[tuple[str, float]]) -> bool`: first validate every key/cost. Coalesce repeated keys by summing costs. At ONE common time, advance/refill all referenced buckets. If every total cost is affordable, subtract all totals and return True. Otherwise return False and subtract nothing from any bucket. A denied batch still retains the refill/time advance and creation of referenced buckets. Summed costs in tests remain finite. Empty list returns True.

Every valid call to these four RateLimiter methods samples the injected clock exactly once, including empty batches. Validate all key/cost arguments BEFORE sampling or making changes. The sampled time must be numeric, finite, and >= the last successfully accepted clock sample across ALL keys/operations. Invalid/backward samples raise `ValueError` and leave every bucket and the previous accepted sample unchanged. Failed affordability is a normal result, so its clock sample is accepted. A first sample may be any finite number. Invalid configuration, key, or cost must never call the clock. No method modifies the requests list. Separate RateLimiter instances are independent. Use the TokenBucket implementation for refill and token accounting.

## Files
- `token_bucket.py`
- `rate_limiter.py`
